200.title: Poland earmarks over €1 billion to help heavy industry go green
200.summary: Poland’s parliament has approved a 4.8 billion złoty (€1.09 billion) support package to help energy-intensive industries cope with high electricity costs and invest in cleaner technologies. 200.body: Under the new measures, companies receiving state aid must invest at least 50% of the funds in renewable energy. Article no 3226 Poland wants a larger role in nuclear deterrence through both NATO’s U.S.-backed nuclear-sharing arrangements and closer cooperation with France, Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz has said. How NATO Nuclear Sharing Works NATO’s nuclear-sharing arrangements combine U.S. nuclear weapons forward-deployed in Europe with capabilities and infrastructure provided by participating allies. In August, Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski told Reuters that Poland wanted to participate in NATO nuclear deterrence but did not want nuclear warheads on its territory.

200.title: European Values, Poland and Ukraine, by Bohdan Vitvitsky
200.body: The strange historical dispute between Poland and Ukraine, in which Polish officials keep making demands upon Ukraine, seems unwilling to die down. In response, the Polish charge d’affaires in Kyiv, Piotr Lukasiewicz, responded by stating that “glorifying the UPA and criminal figures runs counter to European values and the strategic and neighborly relations between Ukraine and Poland.” Similar statements were then echoed by other Polish officials, including ministers. As a general proposition, it is, thus, contrary to European values for Poland or Polish officials to assume that Poland has some sort a special right to dictate to Ukraine whom it may or may not memorialize, as one can presume that Poland would vigorously reject Ukraine’s or anyone else’s attempt to tell Poland which historical figures it may or may not memorialize based on that outside country’s views of the demerits of Poland’s various heroes.

300.title: WE ARE MAKING UP FOR LOST TIME: POLISH FM ON PM TUSK’S VISIT | The Sunday Guardian - newspaper
300.summary: Here, Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski speaks on the opportunities, the fault lines and the future of the India-Poland partnership.Q: This was the first visit by a Polish Prime Minister to India in 16 years, making it a particularly significant milestone.
300.body: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk arrived in India with a clear agenda: deepen trade, open new doors for defence and technology cooperation, and give India-Poland ties a more strategic edge.But beyond the ceremony and the business deals, bigger questions remain, from Europe’s security and the war in Ukraine to energy politics and Poland's global ambitions. Here, Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski speaks on the opportunities, the fault lines and the future of the India-Poland partnership.Q: This was the first visit by a Polish Prime Minister to India in 16 years, making it a particularly significant milestone. Why did it take so long, and what do you consider the single biggest outcome of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s visit?A: Sixteen years was too long. But visits by Prime Minister Modi, External Affairs Minister Jaishankar, and now Prime Minister Tusk show that we are making up for lost time.

500.title: Anthropic says one AI agent beats many subagents now that models can handle complexity alone
500.body: AI in practice Copy the url to clipboard Share this article Go to comment section Anthropic says one AI agent beats many subagents now that models can handle complexity alone Matthias Bastian View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian Oct 25, 2026 Nano Banana Pro prompted by THE DECODER Key Points Anthropic recommends that companies evaluate whether they can consolidate sub-agents into a single agent that loads context on demand. Ask about this article… Search Anthropic found that a single agent with on-demand context often outperforms multi-agent setups in quality, cost, and latency. In one comparison, Anthropic says the single-agent architecture ran about twice as fast as the multi-agent setup. Ad Anthropic says sub-agents still make sense when a single agent's context window shows measurable performance degradation, when multiple tasks need to run in parallel with separate context windows, or when a single agent struggles with tool selection.

500.title: OpenAI used AI agents to hack its own defenses before resuming model training
500.summary: “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” OpenAI said in a statement.
500.body: OpenAI will train its most advanced AI models without access to the live internet, citing the growing security risks posed by increasingly capable systems that can exploit software vulnerabilities and bypass restrictions designed to contain them. “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” OpenAI said in a statement. A key factor was an incident on September 20, when an internal OpenAI research model exploited a misconfiguration in a DNS resolver to gain limited access to the live internet during a training run. To test its defenses, OpenAI launched a large-scale red-teaming campaign in which teams of AI agents were tasked with finding ways to access the live internet, cross internal security boundaries and communicate with agents from which they were supposed to be isolated.
